events.text:
### Verdict

One clear, repeated defect dominates this batch: offer letters keep rows whose approval value is zero (a "£0" sign-on bonus line, a "0 shares" equity line). The user objected in three of the four sessions, and the one session where both values were non-zero was praised. Everything else (dates, formatting, relocation removal, file names, PDF conversion) held up in every session, so the fix should target zero-value rows, not the whole letter pipeline.

### Coverage

Deep-read all four assigned traces in full: ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542, ses_01a1c5f4, ses_01a1cca8. No counterexamples were sampled from outside the batch; the only trace with a materially different shape (ses_01a1cca8) is in the assignment. Every session was inventoried with one Python pass (tool counts, roles, error text, letter text).

### Findings

1. Zero-value offer rows survive into the letter. Confidence: high. In ses_01a1c4c6 the approval reads "Sign-on bonus £0" and the saved letter still shows "Sign-on Bonus: £0"; the user replied that the £0 line should be left out. In ses_01a1c542 the approval reads "Equity 0 shares" and the letter shows "Equity Grant: 0 shares"; the user asked for that line to be dropped. In ses_01a1cca8 the approval has both at zero and the letter shows both rows, and the user repeated the request. The reply there even advertised "£0 sign-on, 0 shares" as a delivered feature. Outcome: the user verdict is negative in all three.
2. The praise case is the control. ses_01a1c5f4 had £4,000 bonus and 800 shares, and the letter was approved as "exactly it". This supports the zero-value reading rather than a general formatting complaint. Confidence: medium-high.
3. The same defect survived across sessions with feedback in between. ses_01a1c4c6 (10 Nov morning) and ses_01a1c542 (10 Nov midday) each got negative feedback, and ses_01a1cca8 (11 Nov) repeated it. The agent's standing instructions cover dates, run-level filling, conditional blocks, PDF conversion and missing fields, but say nothing about zero-valued fields, and each session rebuilds its own fill script. Confidence: high on the pattern, medium on the cause.
4. The mechanics are visible in the scripts. The three short sessions used an almost identical script (same file, only the values differ) that substitutes the raw approval value into the placeholder, so "0" is printed literally in the table row. Confidence: high.
5. Verification depth is uneven. ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542 and ses_01a1c5f4 never inspected the PDF they shipped; they verified only the DOCX. ses_01a1cca8 converted to PDF, extracted the PDF text, and that is exactly where it noticed the spacing loss ("£52,000per year", "25days") that its own DOCX inspection had missed. Confidence: high.
6. Tool waste concentrated in ses_01a1cca8: 23 shell calls against 8 in the other three, three failed calls (missing unzip, a placeholder assertion on the split "POSTCODE" tag, a tuple-unpack crash), and a bespoke XML-level filler built from scratch although the same-day python-docx approach had already worked three times. It also read two earlier generated letters to infer the relocation-removal convention instead of working from the template. Confidence: high.

### Hypotheses

1. Adding a zero check to the fill step and deleting the whole table row (not just the value) would remove the defect. Disproof: any template row where 0 is meaningful, such as a days field.
2. The defect persists because the standing instructions never mention zero-valued fields, and the fill script is rewritten per session rather than shared. Disproof: a later run in which the same rule set already omits zero rows, or evidence that a session remembered feedback without a written rule.
3. ses_01a1cca8 used more calls because it chose a different technique, not because its approval was harder; its approval had the same fields as the others. Disproof: a comparable approval under the python-docx path needing a similar number of calls.

### Failure taxonomy

STATE_MISMATCH in ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542, ses_01a1cca8 (letter shows zero-valued rows the approval says are absent). TOOL_ERROR three times in ses_01a1cca8, all self-recovered. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for PDF fidelity in the three short sessions, since the PDFs were never read back.

### Tool waste and better paths

Rebuilding a near-identical fill script in each session (ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542, ses_01a1c5f4) is the largest recurring cost; one shared script taking the approval values as input would remove roughly four calls per session. In ses_01a1cca8, unzipping and hand-editing XML, plus two debugging rounds on the split "POSTCODE" tag, could have been avoided with the python-docx method the same day's sessions used. Reading the PDF after conversion is the one step that found a real defect and is missing everywhere else.

### Candidate directions

A standing rule that a field with a zero or none value is omitted entirely, including its table row. One reusable, parameterised fill script stored alongside the template. A fixed verification pass over the converted PDF text, including the zero rows, the salary bold and the deadline underline. A one-line check of the saved DOCX for any literal "0" or "£0" before replying.

### Unresolved

Whether the three short sessions' PDFs had spacing defects like the one found in ses_01a1cca8; their PDFs were never opened. Whether ses_01a1cca8 left an empty paragraph where the relocation block was removed, since its own notes say it copied a spacer convention from an earlier letter. Whether removing the zero rows leaves visible gaps in the compensation table. The batch contains no session where a field was missing from the approval, so the "ask instead of guessing" instruction stays untested here.

events.text:
### Verdict
Across all four offer-letter sessions the agent followed every written rule (date style, run-by-run fill, relocation block removal, PDF conversion, no invented fields). The user rejected three of the four, and in each rejection named one thing the current instruction set does not cover: a detail-table row kept when its approval value is zero (sign-on bonus £0, equity 0 shares). One session additionally shipped a formatting regression the agent itself had detected but did not act on.

### Coverage
Deep-read: ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542, ses_01a1c5f4, ses_01a1cca8 (all assigned; full mode). Inventory-only and sampled counterexamples: none needed; every batch trace was deep-read. Optimizer history (e_001, e_002, e_003) checked; none previously addressed zero-value rows, so the main finding is new, not a relapse of a prior fix.

### Findings
1. Zero-value compensation lines reach the finished letter (confidence: high, 3 of 3 negative sessions). ses_01a1c4c6 approval had no bonus and the letter was built from SIGNING_BONUS '0'; its own reopen step printed "Sign-on Bonus: £0" and the user replied with the thumbs-down about exactly that line. ses_01a1c542 had "Equity Grant: 0 shares"; the user's thumbs-down named equity. ses_01a1c5f4, the only thumbs-up, had both values non-zero (£4,000, 800 shares), so no empty-looking row appeared. The existing conditional-block rule covers {{IF_RELOCATION}} paragraphs but not the fixed salary/bonus/equity table rows, and the run-by-run fill script does not drop them.
2. Stated formatting check overridden by the reply (confidence: medium, single session). In ses_01a1cca8 the reopen check reported the base-salary number with bold: False, yet the closing reply asserted "£52,000 (bold, preserved)". The other three sessions reported bold: True and made the same claim consistently.
3. Two approval fields never left the agent guessing; every rejection was about a present-but-zero value, not a missing one (confidence: medium).

### Hypotheses

events.text:
Short answer: the feedback does not ask for a check, only for the omission, so the extra clause was my inference rather than something the users requested.

What the three rejections actually said. In ses_01a1c4c6 the user wrote "There's a '£0' sign-on bonus line. If there's no bonus, just leave the line out." In ses_01a1c542 the user wrote "Same thing with equity. '0 shares' looks odd, drop the line when there's none." In ses_01a1cca8 the user wrote "There's a '£0' sign-on bonus and '0 shares' of equity again. If the approval has none, leave the line out." Every one of those messages asks only that the line be absent from the letter. None mentions verifying, rechecking, or inspecting the output.

Why I added it anyway. The behavioral observation behind it is real: in ses_01a1c4c6 the agent reopened the saved letter and its own printout showed the row "Sign-on Bonus: | £0", and it still delivered. ses_01a1cca8 likewise delivered with "Sign-on Bonus:£0" and "Equity Grant:0 shares" visible in its final summary. So the omission rule has to be applied before the delivery check, not merely checked for. That is a reasonable argument for putting the zero check next to the existing reopen step, since the file already tells agents to reopen and check the salary and deadline formatting.

Why it is still weaker than the omission rule. The instruction to keep only proven signals cuts against me here. The existing reopen bullet already requires reopening the saved file, so the marginal value of my extra clause is low, and it is the one part of my proposal that no user asked for and no rejected output demonstrates as needed. The accepted session, ses_01a1c5f4, had a real bonus and share count, so no session in this batch has ever delivered a letter with the row deleted, and the look of the compensation table after removal is unverified.

My recommendation is to keep the single rule about zero values meaning not offered with the whole table row deleted, and drop the addition to the reopen step. If you want one change on the record rather than two, that is the version I would stand behind.

I do not see a need for the second edit based on this feedback. The user in ses_01a1c4c6 asked for the £0 sign-on bonus line to be left out, in ses_01a1c542 asked for the 0 shares line to be dropped, and in ses_01a1cca8 asked for both lines to be left out when the approval has none. None of them asked for an additional verification step.

The proposed zero-value rule already says to delete the whole table row, and the existing reopen-and-check step is about the saved file being correct before replying. Folding the zero check into that step would mostly repeat the new rule at check time rather than add a distinct behavior. It could be defensible as a safeguard, since the agents did see the zero lines when they reopened the letters, but the feedback itself does not show that a separate check is needed. I would keep the smaller proposal.
